# What each state draws

<!-- Generated by tools/shield-matrix.mjs. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every cell below is the design the style expression actually produces for
that input, obtained by evaluating the expression rather than by describing
it. Regenerate with `node tools/shield-matrix.mjs > docs/shield-matrix.md`.

## The rules, which do not vary by state

### OSM / Protomaps — the road carries `network`

| network | design | why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `US:I` | `interstate` | the interstate is the interstate everywhere |
| `US:US` | `us` | likewise the US route |
| `US:US:Business` | `us-business` | a banner is a plate on the same shield |
| `US:MI` | `st-MI` | the state's own marker |
| `US:MI:Business` | `st-MI-business` | banner: still the state, wearing a plate |
| `US:MI:Secondary` | `st-MI` | a third component that is not a banner |
| `US:MI:County` | `county` | likewise |
| `US:MI:Orange` | `county` | likewise — a county named rather than labelled |
| `(absent)` | `circle` | nothing says who numbered it |

Banner words, the closed set the rule is built on: `alternate`, `business`, `bypass`, `connector`, `loop`, `scenic`, `spur`, `truck`.

### Mapbox — the road carries `shield`, a marker *shape*

| shield | design, map over Michigan | design, map over Tennessee |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `us-interstate` | `interstate` | `interstate` |
| `us-highway` | `us` | `us` |
| `us-state` | `st-MI` | `st-TN` |
| `circle-white` | `st-MI` | `st-TN` |
| `diamond-white` | `st-MI` | `st-TN` |
| `something-unprobed` | `st-MI` | `st-TN` |
| `default` | `circle` | `circle` |
| `(absent)` | `circle` | `circle` |

The two columns differ for every shape because the Mapbox schema never says
whose road it is. The marker is the state the **viewport** is over, which is
right until the screen holds two states.

## Per state

`Secondary` is the column to read. It means two different things and the
word cannot tell you which: Virginia and West Virginia use it for a system
of its own - the circle-signed roads a county numbers - while Michigan and
Tennessee use it for their own state routes, the ones that are not trunk or
primary. BUS M 60 is a Michigan state route.

So it is a per-state fact held in a list, and the list is short on purpose:
it holds only the states somebody has actually looked at. A state showing
`county` below has not been checked, not been ruled on. If its secondaries
are really state routes, say so and it gets added.

The conservative direction is deliberate. A state route drawn in a plain
circle is wrong and obviously generic; a county road wearing the state
shield asserts something false about the road.
